audit.why: Cassiopeia 58.18% over 165 games. The page already frames it as her lane from level 2 with Jax reclaiming it on items, which matches both layers' phase sides (Skill at 4-5 and first item).
audit.corrected: No side changes. Language tightened only.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate was called 'Grandmaster's Might' in four places (spikes[3].text, late, whys[6], wants.foe[2]). That is the pre-rework name.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon gives Jax R as Grandmaster-at-Arms, 110/100/90s. A wrong ult name on the item-spike line undercuts the whole late-game section.
audit.corrected: All four now read Grandmaster-at-Arms, and the spike line carries Counter Strike's 9s max-rank cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer stated that Counter Strike dodges attacks but not abilities, and 'Twin Fangs' was pluralised. The full layer's cooldown block had no numbers at all.
audit.why: Riot: Counter Strike lets Jax 'dodge all incoming attacks'. Twin Fang is an ability, not an attack, so Cassiopeia's entire damage pattern goes straight through the dodge window — that is the decisive interaction and the page told the player to stop casting instead. Miasma grounding disables Leap Strike (Riot: 'Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities'; Leap Strike is a dash).
audit.corrected: Counter Strike's attack-only dodge and Miasma-vs-Leap-Strike now appear in content.mid, full.report[5].t, full.breakdown.cooldowns, full.loading and full.dosFull[2].d. Twin Fang singularised.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every window was written as 'once the dodge expires' with no duration.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 down to 9s at rank 5; Leap Strike is 8s at rank 1; Miasma is 24s at rank 1. Those three numbers are the lane's clock.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into content.mid, full.breakdown.cooldowns, full.dosFull[0].d and full.loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never said Petrifying Gaze only stuns targets that face Cassiopeia.
audit.why: Riot: it stuns 'enemies in front of her that are facing her' and only slows those with their back turned. Jax leaping at you is automatically facing you, which is why the R is a clean answer to his engage and a bad answer to his retreat.
audit.corrected: Facing rule written into full.loading and full.report[5].t.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze answers his Leap Strike all-in: when he Q's onto you, face him, stun, and chain Twin Fangs while his E Counter Strike whiffs on nothing.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze answers his Leap Strike all-in: he faces you to leap, so R stuns, then chain Twin Fang — Counter Strike dodges autos, never your E.

edits.before: Jax's window — Trinity Force and Grandmaster's Might resistances let him eat your poison and all-in through a single missed W, so one Leap-Strike-into-E-stun chain can delete you.
edits.after: Jax's window — Trinity Force and Grandmaster-at-Arms resistances let him eat your poison and all-in through one missed W, so a Leap-Strike-into-E-stun chain on its 9s cooldown deletes you.

edits.before: This is your lane. Hold W (Miasma) for the moment he Leap Strikes at you — the ground disables the dash mid-animation and leaves him stranded in your poison cloud while you back off and chain Twin Fangs. Bait his E: when he pops Counter Strike, walk out of melee and keep poking with Q, then re-engage once the dodge expires. At 6, if he goes for the Leap Strike all-in, face him and R to stun him solid, then Twin-Fang him down — he has no escape once he's grounded and locked.
edits.after: This is your lane. Hold W (Miasma) for the moment he casts Leap Strike — grounding kills the dash mid-flight and strands him in your poison while you back off and chain Twin Fang. Counter Strike dodges attacks, not abilities: when he pops it, step out of melee but keep poking with Q and E, then commit on its 17-second rank-1 cooldown. At 6, face his Leap Strike and R to stun him solid, then Twin-Fang him down — grounded and locked, he has no exit.

edits.before: This is where Jax reclaims it, so close the lane before he gets there. Once he finishes Trinity Force and has Grandmaster's Might resists up, he tanks your poison through the armor/MR and all-ins through a single misplaced W — and you have no defensive steroid beyond your passive speed. One Leap-Strike-into-E-stun chain deletes you. Snowball your level 2-6 window into a lead and end before his item spikes flip the duel; in the late teamfight, save W to ground his engage and R to lock him the instant he leaps onto your carries.
edits.after: This is where Jax reclaims it, so close the lane before he gets there. Once he finishes Trinity Force and has Grandmaster-at-Arms resists up, he tanks your poison through the armour/MR and all-ins through one misplaced W — and you have no defensive steroid beyond your passive speed. A Leap-Strike-into-E-stun chain deletes you. Snowball your level 2-6 window into a lead and end before his item spikes flip the duel; in the late teamfight, save W to ground his engage and R to lock him the instant he leaps onto your carries.

edits.before: Jax out-scales hard: Trinity Force and Grandmaster's Might resistances let him tank your poison and all-in through one missed W — play safe and let your stun peel him.
edits.after: Jax out-scales hard: Trinity Force and Grandmaster-at-Arms resistances let him tank your poison and all-in through one missed W — play safe and let your stun peel him.

edits.before: Stall to Trinity Force plus Grandmaster's Might so his resistances tank your poison and he all-ins through you
edits.after: Stall to Trinity Force plus Grandmaster-at-Arms so his resistances tank your poison and he all-ins through you

edits.before: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Miasma has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Jax Counter Strike: 17s at rank 1, 9s at max — it dodges attacks, not your Twin Fang, so keep casting through it and commit the moment it ends. - Miasma is 24s at rank 1: spend it on his 8s Leap Strike, nothing else. - Petrifying Gaze is 120s.

edits.before: Track Jax’s Counter Strike: Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Miasma grounds Leap Strike. Counter Strike dodges attacks, not Twin Fang — keep casting E and stun him as he faces you.

edits.before: - Cassiopeia vs Jax - Track: Jax Counter Strike. - E only poisoned targets — mana is the lane. - No commits into Counter Strike. - The ultimate closes arguments; it doesn’t open them.
edits.after: - Cassiopeia vs Jax - Track: Counter Strike, 17s at rank 1. - E only poisoned targets — mana is the lane. - W grounds Leap Strike. - Face him and R stuns; turn away and it slows.

edits.before: Dodges every auto and stuns — hold your damage until it ends. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Leap Strike is 8s at rank 1 — hold Miasma for it, and the grounding strands him in your poison.

edits.before: Jax burns Counter Strike on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Jax burns Counter Strike on nothing — Twin Fang was never dodgeable by it.

notes: Internal contradiction left alone rather than guessed at: full.phases[6] gives '2+ items' to Cassiopeia while content.spikes[3] and content.late both give the late game to Jax. content.win[6] agrees with the full layer (Cassiopeia). Also note the full layer's phase 'why' strings are generic boilerplate shared across Cassiopeia's whole matchup table (identical wording appears vs Jayce, Karma, Kayle and others) and mention neither Jax nor Counter Strike; that is a champion-wide template problem, not a Jax one.
